nl.location: 📍 Bij Katwoude, tussen Monnickendam en Volendam · Rietland · Klein
nl.description: Het Rietland Katwoude ligt buitendijks aan het Markermeer, en de naam van het dorp verwijst naar het woud dat hier ooit op het veen groeide. Het rietland zelf is jonger: het ontstond na de afsluiting van de Zuiderzee in 1932, toen het brakke water zoet werd en riet zich massaal langs de oevers kon vestigen. Dat proces heeft langs het hele Markermeer een rietgordel opgeleverd die er in de zoute tijd niet was. Nu staat die gordel onder druk: doordat het peil kunstmatig vlak wordt gehouden verjongt het riet niet meer, en het slaat om in ruigte. Waar het riet nog goed is, broeden roerdomp, snor, baardman en rietzanger; in de winter jagen er blauwe kiekendieven en velduilen.

tags: Reedland · foreland marsh on the Markermeer
en.location: 📍 Near Katwoude, between Monnickendam and Volendam · Reedland · Small
en.description: The Rietland Katwoude lies outside the dike on the Markermeer, and the village name refers to the woud, forest, that once grew here on the peat. The reedland itself is younger: it arose after the closing of the Zuiderzee in 1932, when the brackish water turned fresh and reed could establish along the banks on a huge scale. That process produced a reed belt along the entire Markermeer that did not exist in the salt era. Now that belt is under pressure: because the water level is kept artificially flat the reed no longer rejuvenates and turns to rough vegetation. Where the reed is still good, bittern, Savi’s warbler, bearded reedling and sedge warbler breed; in winter hen harriers and short-eared owls hunt there.

nl.description: Het Heitje van Katham is een curiositeit: een piepklein stukje heide midden in het veenweidegebied van Waterland, waar heide eigenlijk niet thuishoort. De verklaring zit in de bodem. Op deze plek ligt een zandopduiking — waarschijnlijk opgebracht zand of een oude zandkop — die net boven het veen uitsteekt en dus zure, droge en voedselarme omstandigheden biedt. Precies die drie factoren zijn wat struikheide nodig heeft. Katham zelf combineert kat, mogelijk van een oude persoonsnaam of van kate (kleine woning), met ham, de bekende term voor een bocht land in het water. Op het heitje groeien struikheide, buntgras en korstmossen, en er vliegen heidevlinders en graafbijen.

tags: Poor grassland · sand outcrop in the peat landscape
en.location: 📍 Near Katham, close to Monnickendam · Poor grassland · Very small
en.description: The Heitje van Katham is a curiosity: a tiny patch of heath in the middle of the peat-meadow country of Waterland, where heath really does not belong. The explanation lies in the soil. At this spot there is a sand outcrop — probably imported sand or an old sandy knoll — that just rises above the peat and so offers acid, dry and nutrient-poor conditions. Those three factors are exactly what ling needs. Katham itself combines kat, possibly from an old personal name or from kate (a small cottage), with ham, the familiar term for a bend of land in the water. On the little heath grow ling, grey hair-grass and lichens, and heath butterflies and mining bees fly here.

nl.location: 📍 Ten noorden van Broek in Waterland · Veenweide · Middelgroot
nl.description: Het Noorderveen hoort bij het veenweidecomplex van Waterland, een streek die zijn naam eer aandoet: hier is meer water dan land, en het veen ligt zo laag dat het onder de zeespiegel is gezakt. Dat bodemdaling is de kern van het Waterlandse probleem — zodra veen wordt ontwaterd, oxideert het en klinkt het in, waardoor het maaiveld daalt en er nog dieper moet worden bemalen. Het is een neerwaartse spiraal die al achthonderd jaar loopt. In het Noorderveen wordt die spiraal bewust omgekeerd: het peil is verhoogd, percelen zijn vernat en er zijn petgaten uitgegraven. Het resultaat is nat grasland met veenmos en rietkragen, waar watersnip, tureluur, rietgors en bruine kiekendief broeden.

tags: Peat meadow · wet grasslands with turf pits
en.location: 📍 North of Broek in Waterland · Peat meadow · Medium-sized
en.description: The Noorderveen belongs to the peat-meadow complex of Waterland, a district that lives up to its name: there is more water than land here, and the peat has sunk so low that it lies below sea level. That subsidence is the core of the Waterland problem — as soon as peat is drained it oxidises and compacts, so the ground level drops and pumping must go deeper still. It is a downward spiral that has been running for eight hundred years. In the Noorderveen that spiral is deliberately reversed: the level has been raised, parcels rewetted and turf pits dug. The result is wet grassland with sphagnum and reed fringes, where snipe, redshank, reed bunting and marsh harrier breed.

nl.location: 📍 Tussen Westzaan en Wormerveer · Veenweide · Middelgroot
nl.description: Het Guisveld is een van de gaafste veenweidegebieden van de Zaanstreek en valt op door zijn extreem smalle percelen: sommige stroken zijn nauwelijks tien meter breed, gescheiden door sloten die je met een stap kunt overbruggen. Dat patroon is het gevolg van eeuwenlange erfdeling — bij elke generatie werd het land in de lengte gesplitst, zodat iedere erfgenaam een gelijk aandeel kreeg van zowel de hoge als de lage grond. Na tien generaties resteren linten in plaats van percelen. Voor moderne landbouw is dat onwerkbaar, en juist daarom is het gebied natuur geworden. Er groeien veenmosrietland en trilveen, en er broeden rietzanger, snor, watersnip en bruine kiekendief. In de sloten leeft de groene glazenmaker.

tags: Peat meadow · narrow strips and reedland in the Zaan district
en.location: 📍 Between Westzaan and Wormerveer · Peat meadow · Medium-sized
en.description: The Guisveld is one of the finest peat-meadow areas of the Zaan district and stands out for its extremely narrow parcels: some strips are barely ten metres wide, separated by ditches you can step across. That pattern results from centuries of inheritance division — with each generation the land was split lengthwise so every heir received an equal share of both the high and the low ground. After ten generations, ribbons remain instead of parcels. For modern farming this is unworkable, and that is exactly why the area has become nature. Sphagnum reedland and quaking fen grow here, and sedge warbler, Savi’s warbler, snipe and marsh harrier breed. The green hawker lives in the ditches.

en.location: 📍 Near Zaandijk, behind the Zaanse Schans · Peat meadow · Small
en.description: The Kalverpolder lies immediately behind the Zaanse Schans, and the contrast is striking: where on one side hundreds of thousands of tourists a year walk past the windmills, on the other lies a quiet peat-meadow area largely reachable only by boat. The name refers to its use as pasture for calves — young stock could be put on the wet, small parcels that were too soft for dairy cows. That light use spared the soil. It is now a mosaic of reedland, wet grasslands and turf pits with sphagnum. Sedge warbler, Savi’s warbler, bearded reedling and snipe breed, and it is habitat for the root vole, a subspecies found only in the Netherlands.

en.description: De Reef and the Westzijderveld together form a green wedge reaching deep into the built-up area of Zaandam. The name reef is related to rif or reep and denotes an elongated, narrow strip — exactly what the area is. The Westzijderveld is so called because it lies on the west side of the Zaan; the Zaan district was traditionally divided into east and west sides. Remarkably, this peat lies in the middle of an industrial area: the Zaan district was the Netherlands’ first industrial region, with hundreds of windmills from the seventeenth century on. Yet this peat remained, too wet to build on. It is now reedland with turf pits, where Savi’s warbler, sedge warbler, bearded reedling and marsh harrier breed.

en.description: The Oostzanerveld is the counterpart of the Westzijderveld, on the east side of the Zaan, and it is one of the last large peat areas close to Amsterdam. The area is squeezed between the A8, the ring road and the built-up zone, and yet it is of European ecological importance: it is a Natura 2000 site for its sphagnum reedlands and quaking fens. Those vegetations are rare because they demand a precise water regime — rainwater on top, no intruding nutrient-rich polder water — and that is hard to achieve in surroundings full of pumping stations and roads. Management therefore turns on isolating the peat. Bittern, Savi’s warbler, bearded reedling and purple heron breed, and the root vole lives here.

tags: Cultural landscape · old marine clay area with breach pools and dikes
en.location: 📍 Between Hoorn, Enkhuizen, Medemblik and Alkmaar · Marine clay landscape · Very large
en.description: West Friesland is the old marine clay region behind the West Frisian Ring Dike, a forty-kilometre dike closed around 1250 and thus one of the oldest surviving hydraulic works in the Netherlands. Following the dike, you keep seeing deep round pools on the inner side: breach pools or wielen, scoured out by water bursting through during dike failures. They are the scars of centuries of struggle against the sea, and because they were too deep to fill in, they remained. Together with the dike verges they now form a network of small nature sites in an otherwise intensively farmed landscape. Amphibians and dragonflies live in the pools, and a poor, flower-rich flora blooms on the verges.

en.location: 📍 Near 't Zand, along the A72/N245 · Road verges · Small
en.description: At ’t Zand broad verges run alongside the road, showing how much natural value infrastructure can hold. Road verges together cover tens of thousands of hectares in the Netherlands, and because they are never fertilised and usually mown twice a year with the cuttings removed, they develop precisely the poor, herb-rich environment that has vanished from farmland. They also work as a linear corridor: species can migrate along them through an otherwise inhospitable landscape. The name ’t Zand refers to the sandy subsoil, raised or naturally present, which makes the verges here especially poor. Knapweed, wild carrot and yarrow grow here, and many wild bees, hoverflies and butterflies fly.

tags: City wood · woodland around a sand-extraction lake
en.location: 📍 Northern edge of Lelystad · Woodland with lake · Medium-sized
en.description: The Zuigerplasbos owes its name to the suction-dredger lake at its centre: a pool created when sand was extracted with a suction dredger for building Lelystad. That is typical of the whole of Flevoland — the polder fell dry in 1957, and everything you see there is younger than that. You would expect little ecologically from a wood barely seventy years old, but the young marine clay is exceptionally fertile, so trees grow twice as fast here as on sandy soils. The result is a surprisingly mature wood with a dense understorey. Goshawk, buzzard, nuthatch and great spotted woodpecker breed, and great crested grebe, cormorant and diving ducks use the lake.

tags: City wood · woodland with ponds on young marine clay
en.location: 📍 Near Lelystad · Woodland with ponds · Small
en.description: The Visvijverbos is one of the smaller woods around Lelystad, laid out with a series of ponds originally intended for angling. What began as a recreational facility has become ecologically more interesting than intended: the ponds now have vegetated banks with reed and water plants, forming a water-rich element in a polder where almost all water flows in straight channels. The transition from wood to water is exactly what many species need — kingfishers require banks with roots to burrow into, dragonflies need sheltered, sunny waterside. Great spotted woodpecker, treecreeper and moorhen also breed, and in winter little grebe and tufted duck are present.

tags: River dune · Pleistocene sand ridge beneath the polder clay
en.location: 📍 Near Lelystad · River dune with poor grassland · Small
en.description: The river dune area near Lelystad is one of the strangest places in Flevoland, for here something ancient pushes up through the young polder floor. Beneath the marine clay lies a Pleistocene landscape some twelve thousand years old, formed at the end of the last ice age when wind blew sand from dry river beds into river dunes. Those dunes were later covered by the sea with clay, but in a few places they just reach the surface. Where that happens everything changes: the soil there is acid, dry and nutrient-poor instead of rich and wet. As a result a sparse vegetation grows here with grey hair-grass, sheep’s sorrel and lichens, and mining bees and tiger beetles fly.

tags: Polder wood · province-named wood on young marine clay
en.location: 📍 South of Lelystad · Polder wood · Medium-sized
en.description: The Overijsselse Hout belongs to a series of woods around Lelystad named after the surrounding provinces — there is also a Gelderse Hout and a Hollandse Hout. That naming is no accident: when Eastern Flevoland was laid out in the 1960s, deliberate reference was made to the provinces bordering the new polder, as if the young land had to give itself an ancestry. The woods themselves are production and recreation woodland on fertile marine clay, with ash, poplar and oak in straight compartments. Seventy years on they are ecologically fully fledged: goshawk, buzzard, long-eared owl, nuthatch and green woodpecker breed, and roe deer and foxes live here. In autumn it is rich in fungi.

tags: Polder wood · recreation wood with clearings
en.location: 📍 South-eastern edge of Lelystad · Polder wood · Medium-sized
en.description: The Gelderse Hout lies against Lelystad and is the city’s most-used urban wood. What makes it interesting is its woodland structure: unlike the crisp production compartments elsewhere in the polder, here clearings, wood edges and solitary trees were deliberately used. Ecologically that is no detail, for most species live not in the wood but on the transitions — the zone where woodland grades into grassland offers both shelter and food, and demonstrably holds more species in the Netherlands than either wood or field alone. Such fringe vegetations were everywhere in the old cultural landscape and have largely vanished. Here they have been recreated. Green woodpecker, nuthatch, redstart and long-eared owl breed, and the fringes flower full of butterflies.

en.location: 📍 Between Lelystad and the Oostvaardersplassen · Nature park · Medium-sized
en.description: Natuurpark Lelystad was created in 1970 on a striking premise: it shows the original European fauna that has died out in the Netherlands. European bison, elk, aurochs-type cattle and Przewalski horses roam spacious grazed enclosures — animals that were a matter of course here thousands of years ago and vanished only through hunting and deforestation. That approach fitted an idea emerging in Flevoland in the same years: that nature can not only be protected but also reassembled. The park thus became a forerunner of the thinking that came to full flower shortly afterwards in the Oostvaardersplassen. Beside the large grazers there is ordinary polder woodland, with goshawk, kingfisher, nuthatch and beaver.

Toen Zuidelijk Flevoland in 1968 droogviel, was dit laaggelegen deel bestemd voor industrie, maar de aanleg werd uitgesteld — en in de tussentijd vulde het gebied zich met water, riet en vogels. Binnen enkele jaren bleek er een moeras van internationale betekenis te zijn ontstaan, met roerdompen, lepelaars en de eerste Nederlandse broedende zeearenden sinds mensenheugenis. De beslissing om het te behouden leidde tot het beroemdste en meest omstreden natuurexperiment van Nederland: begrazing door Heckrunderen, konikpaarden en edelherten zonder bijvoeren, om een natuurlijk systeem na te bootsen. en.location: 📍 Between Lelystad and Almere · Marsh and grassland plain · Very large
en.description: The Oostvaardersplassen came about by accident. When Southern Flevoland fell dry in 1968, this low-lying part was earmarked for industry, but construction was postponed — and in the meantime the area filled with water, reed and birds. Within a few years a marsh of international importance had formed, with bitterns, spoonbills and the first Dutch breeding white-tailed eagles in living memory. The decision to keep it led to the most famous and most contested nature experiment in the Netherlands: grazing by Heck cattle, konik horses and red deer without supplementary feeding, to mimic a natural system. After the severe winters and the public debate, the grazing is now managed more actively. The marsh remains spectacular.

Grote grazers en edelherten trekken erdoorheen, en juist die combinatie van bos en begrazing levert een structuur op die je zelden ziet — open plekken, ruige zomen en dood hout blijven liggen. en.location: 📍 Between Lelystad and the Oostvaardersplassen · Polder wood · Large
en.description: The Hollandse Hout adjoins the Oostvaardersplassen directly, which makes it more than an ordinary polder wood: it is the link between the open marsh and the rest of Flevoland. Large grazers and red deer move through it, and that combination of woodland and grazing produces a structure you rarely see — clearings, rough fringes and dead wood left in place. The last is ecologically crucial: in Europe dead wood is estimated to harbour a third of all woodland-dependent species, from beetles to fungi to woodpeckers. In a wood only seventy years old it is remarkable that so much already stands. White-tailed eagle, goshawk, black woodpecker and nuthatch breed, and red deer, roe deer and foxes roam.

Kampen were the individually reclaimed parcels of the old cultural landscape, in contrast to the communal open fields. As a name in a polder of 1968 it is therefore a deliberate borrowing from the old country. The site itself is grassland with scrub, grazed and thereby varied. It functions as a foraging area for birds from the adjoining marsh: great white egret, grey heron, white-tailed eagle and geese are regularly seen.

Dat was vooruitstrevend, want in de jaren zestig gold het akkerbouwgebied van Flevoland als een productielandschap waarin natuur nauwelijks een plaats had. en.location: 📍 Near Zeewolde, in the De Knar polder · Small elements · Small
en.description: At De Knar lies a series of small landscape elements — copses, tree lines, pools and rough field margins — deliberately placed in the arable land when the polder was laid out. That was progressive, for in the 1960s Flevoland’s arable region was regarded as a production landscape in which nature had scarcely a place. The name knar is dialect and means a knot or unevenness; as a field name it indicates an uneven, hard-to-work piece of ground. It was precisely such spots that received the landscape elements. Ecologically they work as stepping stones: without these copses a bird or bat would have to cross kilometres of bare arable land. Yellowhammer, whitethroat and little owl breed, and the pools hold amphibians and dragonflies.

Lange, doorlopende bosstroken werken namelijk als ecologische verbindingszone: dieren die zich niet over open akkers durven te verplaatsen — vleermuizen, kleine zoogdieren, veel bosvogels — gebruiken ze als route door de polder. Er broeden boomkruiper, zwartkop en grote bonte specht, en langs het water jaagt de ijsvogel.

tags: Polder wood · ribbon wood along a canal
en.location: 📍 Along the Larservaart near Lelystad · Ribbon wood · Small
en.description: The Larservaartbos is a narrow strip of woodland along the Larservaart, and that shape is no accident. When Flevoland was laid out, strips of woodland were planted along the main canals, originally to break the wind: on the bare new polder wind erosion was a real problem, and young crops could literally be blown away. Those shelterbelts are now mature and fulfil a second function they were never intended for. Long, continuous strips of woodland work as an ecological corridor: animals that will not cross open arable land — bats, small mammals, many woodland birds — use them as a route through the polder. Treecreeper, blackcap and great spotted woodpecker breed, and the kingfisher hunts along the water.

nl.description: Het Toppad loopt langs de noordwestkant van Urk, en het is de plek waar je nog kunt zien dat dit ooit een eiland in de Zuiderzee was. Urk ligt op een keileemkop: een restant van de voorlaatste ijstijd, toen het landijs hier keileem afzette — een taaie mengeling van klei, zand en zwerfstenen. Die harde bult weerstond de zee terwijl het omringende veen wegspoelde, en zo bleef Urk over als eiland tot de inpoldering het in 1942 aan het vasteland vastlegde. Langs het Toppad ligt de oude klifrand met keileem en zwerfkeien in de basis. Het is de enige plek in Flevoland met natuurlijk reliëf uit de ijstijd. Langs de dijk trekken steltlopers en meeuwen, en op het water zitten ’s winters duikeenden.

en.description: The Toppad runs along the north-west side of Urk, and it is the place where you can still see that this was once an island in the Zuiderzee. Urk sits on a boulder-clay knoll: a remnant of the penultimate ice age, when the land ice deposited boulder clay here — a tough mixture of clay, sand and erratic stones. That hard hump resisted the sea while the surrounding peat washed away, and so Urk survived as an island until the reclamation attached it to the mainland in 1942. Along the Toppad lies the old cliff edge with boulder clay and erratics at its base. It is the only place in Flevoland with natural ice-age relief. Waders and gulls pass along the dike, and diving ducks use the water in winter.

nl.description: Schokland was tot 1859 een bewoond eiland in de Zuiderzee, en het is het eerste Nederlandse UNESCO-werelderfgoed (1995). Het verhaal is aangrijpend: het eiland kromp door de zee eeuwenlang, tot het nog maar een paar honderd meter breed was en de bewoners bij elke storm om hun leven vreesden. In 1859 besloot de regering het te ontruimen — de bevolking werd verplicht verhuisd. Sinds de inpoldering ligt Schokland als een langgerekte verhoging in de vlakke polder, met de kerk en de terpen nog zichtbaar. Rondom is het Schokkerbos aangeplant. Het contrast tussen het eeuwenoude eiland en het jonge bos maakt de plek uniek. Er broeden havik, ransuil en boomklever, en er groeit een rijke paddenstoelenflora.

en.location: 📍 Between Ens and Nagele, Noordoostpolder · Former island with wood · Medium-sized
en.description: Schokland was an inhabited island in the Zuiderzee until 1859, and it is the first Dutch UNESCO World Heritage Site (1995). The story is poignant: the sea shrank the island for centuries, until it was only a few hundred metres wide and the inhabitants feared for their lives in every storm. In 1859 the government decided to evacuate it — the population was compulsorily moved. Since the reclamation Schokland has lain as an elongated rise in the flat polder, with the church and the mounds still visible. Around it the Schokkerbos was planted. The contrast between the ancient island and the young wood makes the place unique. Goshawk, long-eared owl and nuthatch breed, and a rich fungus flora grows.

nl.description: De Kamperhoek is de noordoostelijke punt van Oostelijk Flevoland, waar de polder uitsteekt in het Ketelmeer, en dat maakt de plek tot een van de beste vogeltrekposten van Nederland. Trekvogels volgen liever land dan water, en waar een landtong in open water steekt hopen ze zich op voordat ze de oversteek wagen — het effect dat vogelaars stuwing noemen. Op najaarsdagen met oostenwind trekken hier tienduizenden vinken, leeuweriken en spreeuwen langs. Het aangrenzende Ketelbos vangt de vogels op die neerstrijken. Behalve trek is er ook broedvogelrijkdom: havik, buizerd, ijsvogel en zwarte specht, en op het Ketelmeer overwinteren duikeenden en zaagbekken.

en.location: 📍 North-eastern tip of Eastern Flevoland, on the Ketelmeer · Wood and shore · Medium-sized
en.description: The Kamperhoek is the north-eastern tip of Eastern Flevoland, where the polder juts into the Ketelmeer, and that makes it one of the best migration watchpoints in the Netherlands. Migrants prefer to follow land rather than water, and where a spit of land projects into open water they pile up before daring the crossing — the effect birders call funnelling. On autumn days with an easterly wind, tens of thousands of chaffinches, skylarks and starlings pass here. The adjoining Ketelbos catches the birds that drop in. Besides migration there is breeding richness: goshawk, buzzard, kingfisher and black woodpecker, and diving ducks and sawbills winter on the Ketelmeer.

nl.description: Onder de vlakke bodem van Flevoland liggen rivierduinen: zandruggen die aan het einde van de laatste ijstijd zijn ontstaan. Toen was Nederland een koude toendra zonder bosbedekking, en de rivieren voerden ’s zomers smeltwater en zand aan dat in de winter droogviel. De westenwind blies dat zand op tot lange duinen langs de rivierdalen. Later verdronk het gebied onder veen en zeeklei, en de duinen raakten begraven — maar bij Dronten liggen ze zo hoog dat ze na de inpoldering weer aan de oppervlakte kwamen. Op de zandkoppen groeit een schralere vegetatie dan op de omringende klei: dat verschil, in een polder waar alles vlak en gelijk lijkt, is verrassend. Er komen zandbijen, veldleeuwerik en geelgors voor.

tags: River dune · buried ice-age dune in the polder
en.location: 📍 Near Dronten, Eastern Flevoland · River dune · Small
en.description: Beneath Flevoland’s flat floor lie river dunes: sand ridges formed at the end of the last ice age. The Netherlands was then cold tundra without tree cover, and in summer the rivers carried meltwater and sand that fell dry in winter. The westerly wind blew that sand up into long dunes along the river valleys. Later the area drowned beneath peat and marine clay and the dunes were buried — but near Dronten they lie so high that they returned to the surface after the reclamation. On the sandy knolls a poorer vegetation grows than on the surrounding clay: that difference, in a polder where everything looks flat and uniform, is surprising. Mining bees, skylark and yellowhammer occur.

tags: Landart · zonnewende-observatorium van aarde en hout
nl.location: 📍 Swifterbant, tussen Lelystad en Dronten · Landart · Klein
nl.description: Het Observatorium van de Amerikaanse kunstenaar Robert Morris (1977) is een van de bekendste landartwerken van Europa: twee concentrische aarden wallen met een diameter van bijna honderd meter, met stalen en houten poorten. Het is geen sculptuur om naar te kijken maar een instrument. De poorten zijn zo gericht dat de zon op de zonnewendes en de equinoxen precies door de openingen opkomt — hetzelfde principe als Stonehenge, gebouwd in een polder die pas twintig jaar bestond. Morris koos die plek bewust: een volkomen leeg, plat land waar niets de horizon verstoort, zodat de zonsopkomst de enige gebeurtenis is. Op en om de wallen leven graslandvogels en insecten; de wallen zelf zijn schraal begroeid.

tags: Land art · solstice observatory of earth and wood
en.location: 📍 Swifterbant, between Lelystad and Dronten · Land art · Small
en.description: The Observatorium by the American artist Robert Morris (1977) is one of Europe’s best-known works of land art: two concentric earthen ramparts almost a hundred metres across, with steel and wooden gates. It is not a sculpture to look at but an instrument. The gates are aligned so that on the solstices and the equinoxes the sun rises exactly through the openings — the same principle as Stonehenge, built in a polder only twenty years old. Morris chose the site deliberately: a wholly empty, flat land where nothing disturbs the horizon, so that sunrise is the only event. Grassland birds and insects live on and around the ramparts, which carry a sparse sward.

tags: Polder wood · young broadleaf wood by a prehistoric site
en.location: 📍 Near Swifterbant, Eastern Flevoland · Polder wood · Medium-sized
en.description: The Swifterbos lies by Swifterbant, a village that gave its name to the Swifterbant culture — one of the most important archaeological discoveries in the Netherlands. Excavation in the 1960s revealed settlements of people who lived here around 4300–4000 BC on river dunes in what was then a marshy delta. They mark the transition from hunter-gatherers to the first farmers: they already kept livestock and grew grain, yet still fished and hunted extensively. The wood above is young, planted after the reclamation, with ash, maple and poplar. Beneath the soil, then, lie six thousand years of settlement history. Tawny owl, green woodpecker and blackcap breed, and autumn brings a rich fungus flora.

nl.description: Rond Swifterbant ligt een gordel van dorpsbos, en dat is een bewuste ontwerpkeuze van de Rijksdienst voor de IJsselmeerpolders. Elk nieuw polderdorp kreeg een groene mantel: bos direct om de bebouwing heen, bedoeld als windvang, als wandelgebied op loopafstand en als visueel scherm dat het dorp een besloten karakter geeft in een verder eindeloos open landschap. Zonder die mantel zou een polderdorp als een blok in de leegte staan. De bossen zijn inmiddels een halve eeuw oud en volwassen genoeg voor holenbroeders: grote bonte specht, boomklever en bosuil. Voor de dorpsbewoners zijn het de dagelijkse ommetjes; ecologisch werken ze als groene stapstenen tussen de grotere polderbossen.

tags: Village wood · green mantle around a polder village
en.location: 📍 Around Swifterbant · Village wood · Small
en.description: Around Swifterbant lies a belt of village woodland, a deliberate design choice by the IJsselmeer Polders Development Authority. Every new polder village received a green mantle: woodland immediately around the built-up area, intended as a windbreak, as walking country within strolling distance and as a visual screen giving the village an enclosed character in an otherwise endlessly open landscape. Without that mantle a polder village would stand like a block in the void. The woods are now half a century old and mature enough for hole-nesters: great spotted woodpecker, nuthatch and tawny owl. For villagers they are the daily round; ecologically they work as green stepping stones between the larger polder woods.

Dat maakt het aantrekkelijk voor soorten die een rijke bosstructuur nodig hebben: havik, zwarte specht, boomklever en bosuil. Langs het Vossemeer liggen rietoevers waar de zeearend soms wordt gezien, en het bos is bekend om zijn paddenstoelen.

en.description: The Roggebotzand is among the oldest and most varied woods of Eastern Flevoland. The name refers to the Roggebot lock and the shallow in the old Zuiderzee water that lay here. Unlike the rigidly planted production woods elsewhere in the polder, the Roggebotzand has acquired a layered structure: through thinning, natural regeneration and leaving dead wood a wood has grown with glades, dense shrub layers and old trees. That makes it attractive to species needing a rich woodland structure: goshawk, black woodpecker, nuthatch and tawny owl. Along the Vossemeer lie reed shores where the white-tailed eagle is sometimes seen, and the wood is renowned for its fungi.

en.description: The Lage Vaartbos accompanies the Lage Vaart, the principal drainage canal of Eastern Flevoland. That canal is no ornamental waterway but a technical necessity: all surplus water from the polder flows through it to the pumping stations, which lift it over the dike into the IJsselmeer. Without that system the polder would be under water again within weeks. The wood along the canal was planted as a windbreak and bank mantle, and now acts as a long green artery through the arable land. Where wood and water meet, species richness is greatest: kingfisher, water shrew and Daubenton’s bat benefit from the combination. Reed and marsh plants grow along the banks, and blackcap and chiffchaff breed in the wood.

en.description: The Wisentbos is Dronten’s village wood and owes its name to the wisent, the European bison, once kept here in an enclosure as a public attraction. The animals are gone, but the name remained. What makes the wood special is its relief: soil from the canals was used during construction, creating hills, hollows and pools in a landscape that is naturally utterly flat. That artificial variation yields real ecological gain — dry south-facing slopes, wet hollows and shore zones together support far more species than a level wood. Tawny owl, great spotted woodpecker and kingfisher breed, and the ponds hold amphibians and dragonflies.

en.description: Dronten was founded in 1962 as the main town of Eastern Flevoland, and from the outset a green belt belonged to it. The polder’s designers assumed people would not feel at home in a landscape without any shelter; woodland around the settlements was to make the scale of the landscape humane. The village woods of Dronten therefore form a continuous wreath of copses, avenues and green belts you can reach within ten minutes of the built-up area. They are now sixty years old: mature trees, dead wood and shrub layers. That attracts tawny owl, nuthatch, green woodpecker and red squirrel, and the avenues serve as a flight route for bats between town and countryside.

en.description: The Revebos and the Abbertbos together form one of the largest woodland complexes of Eastern Flevoland. The names come from old Zuiderzee grounds: the Rev and the Abbert were shallows and sandbanks that sailors knew and feared, and which now lie dry beneath the wood. They were planted for timber production, but have since been converted into natural woodland: glades, natural regeneration and plenty of dead wood. Sheer continuous area makes the difference here, for species such as goshawk, black woodpecker and pine marten need space. Roe deer are numerous, and orchids flower in the glades on the lime-rich polder soil.

en.description: De Enk is a small wood near Biddinghuizen, and the name is striking: an enk or es is originally an old, elevated arable field on the sandy soils, raised by centuries of manuring with sod manure. In a polder that only fell dry in 1957 no such thing exists — the name was brought along from the east of the country, where many of Flevoland’s first settlers came from. The wood itself is young but varied, with a pond, small open grasslands and mixed broadleaf woodland. It is precisely that small-scale variation within a large-scale polder that makes it rich in species: green woodpecker, nuthatch and kingfisher, and in the pond amphibians and dragonflies.

en.description: Between the villages of Zalk and Wilsum lies one of the most intact stretches of IJssel landscape in Overijssel. The river makes broad bends here and over centuries has left a relief you would not expect in flat surroundings: levees where coarser sand settled during floods, and behind them lower basin soils of heavy clay. The villages and orchards stand on the levees — high and dry — and the basins hold the meadows that flood in winter. That is no accident but the oldest spatial principle of the river district. The floodplains matter for meadow birds and wintering geese, and river-valley flora grows on the dikes and levees.

en.description: The Larserbos is one of the large woods of Southern Flevoland, planted in the 1970s when the polder had only just fallen dry. The planting followed a principle repeated all over Flevoland: first fast-growing poplar and willow as a pioneer crop, since they tolerate the wet, salty young soil, and only under their shelter could ash, maple and oak follow. Thus in thirty years a wood was made that nature would have taken thousands of years to build. It is now layered enough for goshawk, hobby and black woodpecker. In the glades and along the woodland edges orchids flower in June on the lime-rich marine clay — a surprise in a planted wood.

nl.description: Het Biddingbos ligt tussen Biddinghuizen en het Veluwemeer, en het is een van de bossen waar de bodemverschillen van de polder goed zichtbaar zijn. Onder Oostelijk Flevoland liggen naast elkaar zware zeeklei, oude veenlagen en zandige ruggen — restanten van het landschap dat vóór de Zuiderzee bestond. Waar de klei zwaar is groeit het bos traag en blijft het open; op de zandiger plekken staat het dichter. Dat mozaïek geeft variatie die de aanplanters niet hebben ontworpen maar die de ondergrond hun oplegde. Er broeden havik, bosuil en grote bonte specht, en langs de waterpartijen jaagt de ijsvogel. In de herfst is het bos rijk aan paddenstoelen.

en.location: 📍 Near Biddinghuizen, Eastern Flevoland · Polder wood · Medium-sized
en.description: The Biddingbos lies between Biddinghuizen and the Veluwemeer, and is one of the woods where the polder’s soil differences are clearly visible. Beneath Eastern Flevoland lie heavy marine clay, old peat layers and sandy ridges side by side — remnants of the landscape that existed before the Zuiderzee. Where the clay is heavy the wood grows slowly and stays open; on the sandier spots it stands denser. That mosaic gives a variation the planters never designed but which the subsoil imposed on them. Goshawk, tawny owl and great spotted woodpecker breed, and the kingfisher hunts along the pools. In autumn the wood is rich in fungi.

nl.description: Rond Biddinghuizen ligt de gebruikelijke groene mantel van de polderdorpen, maar hier heeft die een extra functie gekregen. Het dorp ligt naast Walibi en het evenemententerrein waar jaarlijks grote festivals worden gehouden; het bos vormt daarmee ook een geluidsbuffer en visueel scherm tussen dorp en drukte. Ecologisch werken de dorpsbossen zoals elders in Flevoland: ze zijn een halve eeuw oud, hebben inmiddels dood hout en struiklagen, en verbinden de grotere polderbossen met elkaar. Er broeden groene specht, boomklever en bosuil, en de bosranden zijn goed voor vlinders en wilde bijen. Voor het dorp zelf zijn het de dagelijkse wandelrondjes.

tags: Village wood · green mantle around a polder village
en.location: 📍 Around Biddinghuizen · Village wood · Small
en.description: Around Biddinghuizen lies the usual green mantle of the polder villages, but here it has acquired an extra function. The village adjoins Walibi and the events ground where large festivals are held each year; the wood therefore also serves as a noise buffer and visual screen between village and bustle. Ecologically the village woods work as elsewhere in Flevoland: half a century old, now with dead wood and shrub layers, and linking the larger polder woods together. Green woodpecker, nuthatch and tawny owl breed, and the woodland edges are good for butterflies and wild bees. For the village itself they are the daily walking round.

tags: Landschapselementen · singels, bosjes en bermen in de polder
nl.location: 📍 Verspreid over Flevoland · Kleine elementen · Verspreid
nl.description: Verspreid over heel Flevoland ligt een fijnmazig net van landschapselementen: erfbeplantingen, houtsingels, bermen, tochtoevers en kleine bosjes. Ze zijn bij de inrichting van de polder ontworpen door landschapsarchitecten van de Rijksdienst voor de IJsselmeerpolders, die als een van de eersten ter wereld natuur en landschap systematisch in een landbouwplan opnamen. Het resultaat is opvallend: een van de meest grootschalige landbouwgebieden van Nederland bezit tegelijk een verrassend dicht netwerk van kleine natuur. Juist die kleine elementen dragen de biodiversiteit van het boerenland — steenuil, geelgors, patrijs, wilde bijen en vlinders zijn er van afhankelijk, en ze verbinden de grote bossen en moerassen met elkaar.

tags: Landscape elements · tree lines, copses and verges in the polder
en.location: 📍 Scattered across Flevoland · Small elements · Scattered
en.description: Scattered across the whole of Flevoland lies a fine-meshed net of landscape elements: farmyard plantings, tree lines, verges, ditch banks and small copses. They were designed when the polder was laid out by landscape architects of the IJsselmeer Polders Development Authority, among the first in the world to incorporate nature and landscape systematically into an agricultural plan. The result is striking: one of the most large-scale farming regions in the Netherlands also possesses a surprisingly dense network of small-scale nature. It is precisely those small elements that carry the biodiversity of the farmland — little owl, yellowhammer, grey partridge, wild bees and butterflies depend on them, and they link the large woods and marshes together.

Op de zware zeeklei van Flevoland was greppelen in de eerste jaren na de drooglegging onmisbaar: de bodem klonk nog in, water bleef staan en zonder afvoer verzuurde het land. Waar de greppels bleven liggen ontstond iets onverwachts: een patroon van natte laagtes en drogere ruggen op korte afstand, precies de gradiënt waarop veel planten en insecten gedijen. Er groeit moerasflora in de greppels en schralere kruiden op de ruggen, met weidevogels, wilde bijen en libellen.

tags: Nature field · furrows and rough ground in polder land
en.location: 📍 Near Zeewolde, Southern Flevoland · Wet field · Small
en.description: The Greppelveld owes its name to the furrows that cut across the site — shallow channels made by hand or plough to lead surplus rainwater to the ditch. On Flevoland’s heavy marine clay, furrowing was indispensable in the first years after drainage: the soil was still settling, water stood, and without drainage the land turned sour. Where the furrows remained something unexpected arose: a pattern of wet hollows and drier ridges at close range, precisely the gradient on which many plants and insects thrive. Marsh flora grows in the furrows and sparser herbs on the ridges, with meadow birds, wild bees and dragonflies.

De naam verwijst niet naar Engeland alleen als stijl maar ook naar het feit dat het terrein tegelijk een waterstaatswerk was: het park lag op de kribben en kaden die de IJssel in bedwang moesten houden, en de aanleg als wandelpark was er handig aan opgehangen. Zo ontstond een unieke combinatie van cultuurhistorie en rivierdynamiek. Het park heeft nu oude bomen, en in de uiterwaarden foerageren ganzen, ijsvogels en steltlopers.

tags: Floodplain park · landscape park on the IJssel
en.location: 📍 South-western edge of Zwolle, on the IJssel · Floodplain park · Medium-sized
en.description: Het Engelse Werk lies in the floodplains near Zwolle and is one of the oldest public parks in the Netherlands: it was laid out around 1830 in the English landscape style, with winding paths, tree clumps and framed views. The name refers not only to England as a style but also to the fact that the site was simultaneously a hydraulic engineering work: the park lay on the groynes and quays meant to keep the IJssel in check, and its creation as a promenade was conveniently attached to that. So arose a unique combination of cultural history and river dynamics. The park now has old trees, and geese, kingfishers and waders feed in the floodplains.

tags: Landscape elements · tree lines along a peat-reclamation ribbon
en.location: 📍 Schuinesloot near Slagharen · Small elements · Small
en.description: Schuinesloot is a ribbon village on a wijk: a dug channel from the era of raised-bog reclamation. The name is literal — the ditch runs at a slant to the surrounding reclamation grid, something immediately striking in the rectilinear peat-colony landscape and pointing to an older course. Along the ribbon lie tree lines, farmyard plantings and verges that arose because every smallholder edged his narrow strip of land with wood — for fuel, utility timber and shelter. What began as farming practice is now the ecological backbone of this open district: little owl, yellowhammer, linnet and many insects depend on it.

Een slag is een langgerekte kavel, gemeten vanaf een ontginningsbasis en tot een vaste diepte het veen in — vandaar dat het landschap bestaat uit smalle, evenwijdige stroken land, gescheiden door sloten. Dit slagenlandschap is honderden jaren oud en verraadt in één blik hoe middeleeuwse boeren het moeras stap voor stap in cultuur brachten. Daarvan profiteren weidevogels, amfibieën en moerasplanten, en langs de kavelsloten broeden rietzangers.

tags: Peat meadow · strip landscape with ditches and tree lines
en.location: 📍 Near Dedemsvaart and Balkbrug · Strip landscape · Medium-sized
en.description: De Slagen is named after the way the peat was reclaimed here. A slag is an elongated parcel, measured from a reclamation base and running a fixed depth into the bog — hence the landscape consists of narrow, parallel strips of land separated by ditches. This strip landscape is centuries old and reveals at a glance how medieval farmers brought the marsh into cultivation step by step. The many ditches and field margins make the area exceptionally rich in edges: proportionally there is an enormous amount of transition between wet and dry. Meadow birds, amphibians and marsh plants benefit, and sedge warblers breed along the parcel ditches.
en.meta: Best season & peak months: Mar–Jun (meadow birds and ditch flora) Best time of day: Early morning — meadow birds calling above the strips.

en.description: Around Zuidwolde lie small copses on and around the old essen — the elevated arable fields of the Drenthe es villages. An es is not a natural hill but a human-made soil: for centuries farmers carried sods from the heath, mixed with stable manure, onto their fields, so that the ground rose centimetres year after year. Some essen therefore lie more than a metre above the surrounding surface. The copses on the es edges and steep banks arose where ploughing became impossible: on the steepest parts. They are now valuable as small woodland reserves with old oaks, and house little owl, green woodpecker and badger.

en.location: 📍 Near Bergentheim, Vecht valley · Heath and wood · Small
en.description: The Nolderveld is a remnant of the extensive heathlands that covered most of eastern Netherlands into the nineteenth century. That heath was no wilderness but a working landscape: farmers grazed sheep on it and cut sods for the byre. When artificial fertiliser made sod manure superfluous, the heath lost its function and almost all of it was reclaimed or planted with trees. What remains are scraps such as the Nolderveld. The name nol means height or sandy knoll — an indication that this was drier and higher than the surrounding peat. Heather grows with self-sown pines, and common lizard, stonechat and woodlark occur.

tags: Heath and pools · wet heath with small bogs
en.location: 📍 Near Zuidwolde, south-west Drenthe · Wet heath · Medium-sized
en.description: The Takkenhoogte is a small but remarkable reserve of wet heath, pools and small bogs on a cover-sand ridge. What makes it special is the impermeable layer in the subsoil: loam or iron pan holds the rainwater, so that in the middle of a sand ridge — where you would expect drought — permanently wet spots occur. That phenomenon is called a perched water table, and it is why bog formation began here. Sphagnum, round-leaved sundew and cranberry grow in the bogs, plants of extremely nutrient-poor conditions. Moor frog, smooth snake and common lizard occur, along with dragonflies such as the white-faced darter.

nl.description: De Ommerschans is een van de best bewaarde zeventiende-eeuwse schansen van Nederland. Ze werd rond 1628 gebouwd in een uitgestrekt onbegaanbaar moeras, op de enige plek waar een doorwaadbare route van oost naar west liep: wie het moeras wilde passeren moest langs de schans. Dat was strategisch bedoeld tegen invallen vanuit het oosten tijdens de Tachtigjarige Oorlog. Later kreeg het terrein een tweede leven als bedelaarsgesticht van de Maatschappij van Weldadigheid — in 2021 opgenomen in de UNESCO-werelderfgoedlijst van de Koloniën van Weldadigheid. tags: Sconce · seventeenth-century fortification in the marsh
en.location: 📍 Between Ommen and Balkbrug · Historic sconce · Small
en.description: The Ommerschans is one of the best-preserved seventeenth-century sconces in the Netherlands. It was built around 1628 in an extensive impassable marsh, at the only spot where a fordable route ran from east to west: anyone wishing to cross the marsh had to pass the sconce. That was strategic, aimed against incursions from the east during the Eighty Years’ War. Later the site had a second life as a beggars’ colony of the Society of Benevolence — added in 2021 to the UNESCO World Heritage list of the Colonies of Benevolence. The ramparts and moats are now grown with old trees; tawny owl, green woodpecker and kingfisher breed.

tags: Landscape elements · tree lines and copses in a peat reclamation
en.location: 📍 Rheezerveen near Hardenberg · Small elements · Small
en.description: Rheezerveen arose as a peat-reclamation village: where the raised bog behind the es of Rheeze was dug away, smallholders settled in the nineteenth century on the exposed sandy subsoil. That ground was poor — what remains after peat cutting is dalgrond, a mixture of sand and peat residue that became productive only with much manure. The farmers edged their parcels with tree lines and alder rows, partly for shelter from the wind over the bare bog, partly for utility timber. Those lines now form a fine-meshed network in an otherwise open landscape, with little owl, yellowhammer, whitethroat and many insects on the flowery verges.

tags: Town on the Vecht · green riverside margins
en.location: 📍 Hardenberg on the Overijsselse Vecht · Town edge and riverbank · Medium-sized
en.description: Hardenberg lies on the Overijsselse Vecht, and that is no ordinary river: it is one of the few Dutch rivers fed not by meltwater but purely by rainfall. The Vecht therefore reacts quickly and violently to precipitation — a rain river with strongly fluctuating levels, which formerly carried sand and threw up river dunes along its banks. The town owes its name to a castle on a hard sandy knoll by that river. Along the town margins lie green banks, floodplains and parks where river dynamics are being given room again through remeandering. Kingfisher, sand martin and little ringed plover breed, and the beaver has returned.

en.location: 📍 On the edge of Hardenberg · Recreational wood · Medium-sized
en.description: The recreational wood of Hardenberg was laid out in the 1960s and 1970s on former heath and waste ground, in an era when the government systematically had town-edge woods planted. Behind that policy lay a social motive: the five-day working week and the car gave ordinary families mass leisure time for the first time, and green space within cycling distance of the town was needed. Such woods were therefore designed with footpaths, ponds and play meadows. Ecologically they have become valuable: sixty years old, with dead wood, shrub layers and older conifer stands. Tawny owl, great spotted woodpecker and goshawk breed, and the ponds attract dragonflies and amphibians.

nl.description: Het Engelandsche Bosch heeft een naam die verwarring wekt: hij verwijst niet naar Engeland maar naar het oude woord eng of enk — hooggelegen bouwland, zoals in de Drentse en Twentse esdorpen. Het bos ligt dan ook op en rond een oude eng bij Rheeze, op een dekzandrug boven het natte Vechtdal. De rechte lanen die het bos doorsnijden verraden een negentiende-eeuwse landgoedaanleg: eigenaren van bezittingen in het Vechtdal lieten hun heidevelden bebossen en er lanenstelsels doorheen leggen, deels voor houtopbrengst, deels als statussymbool. Nu staan er oude beuken en eiken, met boomklever, bosuil, holenduif en in de herfst veel paddenstoelen.

tags: Estate wood · old broadleaf wood with avenues
en.location: 📍 Near Rheeze, south of Hardenberg · Estate wood · Medium-sized
en.description: The Engelandsche Bosch has a name that causes confusion: it refers not to England but to the old word eng or enk — elevated arable land, as in the es villages of Drenthe and Twente. The wood accordingly lies on and around an old eng near Rheeze, on a cover-sand ridge above the wet Vecht valley. The straight avenues cutting through the wood betray a nineteenth-century estate layout: owners of properties in the Vecht valley had their heathlands planted with trees and avenue systems laid through them, partly for timber, partly as a status symbol. Old beeches and oaks now stand there, with nuthatch, tawny owl, stock dove and many fungi in autumn.

nl.location: 📍 Ten oosten van Hardenberg · Kleine elementen · Klein
nl.description: Ten oosten van Hardenberg, richting de Duitse grens, ligt een kleinschalig zandlandschap met houtwallen, singels en kleine bosjes. De houtwal is hier het kenmerkende element: een aarden wal met hakhout erop, aangelegd als veekering in een tijd zonder prikkeldraad. Het vee moest van het bouwland worden gehouden, en een wal met dicht hakhout van eik, els en hazelaar was daarvoor de enige praktische oplossing. Elke acht à twaalf jaar werd het hout afgezet voor geriefhout en brandstof, waardoor de wallen eeuwenlang in stand bleven. Ze zijn nu ecologisch waardevol als lijnvormige elementen: das, steenuil, geelgors en hazelworm zijn ervan afhankelijk.

tags: Landscape elements · hedgebanks and tree lines on sand
en.location: 📍 East of Hardenberg · Small elements · Small
en.description: East of Hardenberg, towards the German border, lies a small-scale sandy landscape of hedgebanks, tree lines and small copses. The houtwal or hedgebank is the characteristic element here: an earthen bank topped with coppice, built as stock-proof fencing in an age without barbed wire. Cattle had to be kept off the arable, and a bank with dense coppice of oak, alder and hazel was the only practical solution. Every eight to twelve years the wood was cut for utility timber and fuel, which kept the banks intact for centuries. They are now ecologically valuable as linear elements: badger, little owl, yellowhammer and slow worm depend on them.

nl.location: 📍 Rheeze, ten zuidwesten van Hardenberg · Esdorp en landgoed · Middelgroot
nl.description: Rheeze is een van de oudste nederzettingen van het Vechtdal en toont het klassieke esdorpmodel nog volledig: een es op de hoge zandrug voor het bouwland, groenlanden in het lage Vechtdal voor het hooi, en heidevelden daarachter voor de schapen en de plaggen. Die drieslag was geen keuze maar een noodzaak — het hele systeem draaide op de mest die schapen ’s nachts in de potstal achterlieten, gemengd met heideplaggen en uitgereden over de es. Zonder heide geen mest, zonder mest geen graan. Rond Rheeze liggen bovendien oude landgoedbossen. Er broeden steenuil, groene specht en ijsvogel, en de das is er algemeen.

tags: Es village · old arable dome and estate on the Vecht
en.location: 📍 Rheeze, south-west of Hardenberg · Es village and estate · Medium-sized
en.description: Rheeze is one of the oldest settlements in the Vecht valley and still shows the classic es-village model in full: an es on the high sand ridge for arable, green lands in the low Vecht valley for hay, and heathlands behind for the sheep and the sods. That threefold system was not a choice but a necessity — the whole thing ran on the manure sheep left overnight in the byre, mixed with heather sods and spread over the es. No heath, no manure; no manure, no grain. Around Rheeze lie old estate woods as well. Little owl, green woodpecker and kingfisher breed, and the badger is common.

nl.location: 📍 Van Gramsbergen via Hardenberg en Ommen naar Zwolle · Rivierdal · Zeer groot
nl.description: Het Vechtdal is het brede dal van de Overijsselse Vecht, en het is het meest dynamische zandrivierlandschap van Nederland. De Vecht is een regenrivier: ze wordt niet gevoed door gletsjers of grote stuwmeren maar uitsluitend door neerslag in Duitsland en Twente, waardoor haar afvoer binnen dagen kan verveelvoudigen. Die grillige rivier heeft in het dal rivierduinen opgeworpen — zand dat bij lage waterstanden droogviel en door de wind werd opgestoven. Nergens anders in Nederland liggen zulke duinen midden in een rivierdal. Na eeuwen normalisatie wordt de Vecht sinds 2005 stapsgewijs hermeanderd. Het dal huisvest bever, otter, ijsvogel, oeverzwaluw en zeldzame stroomdalflora.

tags: River valley · rain river with river dunes
en.location: 📍 From Gramsbergen via Hardenberg and Ommen to Zwolle · River valley · Very large
en.description: The Vecht valley is the broad valley of the Overijsselse Vecht, and it is the most dynamic sandy-river landscape in the Netherlands. The Vecht is a rain river: fed not by glaciers or large reservoirs but purely by rainfall in Germany and Twente, so that its discharge can multiply within days. That capricious river has thrown up river dunes in the valley — sand that fell dry at low water and was blown up by the wind. Nowhere else in the Netherlands do such dunes lie in the middle of a river valley. After centuries of canalisation the Vecht has been progressively remeandered since 2005. The valley holds beaver, otter, kingfisher, sand martin and rare river-valley flora.

tags: Landscape elements · tree lines and copses on the bog edge
en.location: 📍 Bruchterveld near Hardenberg · Small elements · Small
en.description: Bruchterveld lies on the edge of what was once the extensive Bruchterveen, a raised bog reaching far across the German border. The word bruch or broek means marshy, boggy land — the same stem found in dozens of place names on the sandy soils. In the nineteenth century the bog was dug away and a village of smallholders appeared on the poor peat-residue soil. They planted tree lines, alder rows and farmyard copses as protection from the wind and as a source of utility timber. Those elements now form the green structure of an otherwise bare reclamation landscape, with little owl, yellowhammer, linnet and many wild bees on the verges.

Rond Ommen was in de achttiende en negentiende eeuw grootschalige zandverstuiving ontstaan doordat te veel heideplaggen waren gestoken en te veel schapen hadden gegraasd: de vegetatie verdween, de wind kreeg vat op het dekzand en hele akkers en zelfs boerderijen raakten ondergestoven. tags: Wood · mixed wood on drift sand and cover sand
en.location: 📍 Near Ommen, Vecht valley · Wood · Medium-sized
en.description: The Ommerbos was planted on former drift sand — which explains both the wood and its soil. Around Ommen large-scale sand drifting arose in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries because too many heather sods had been cut and too many sheep had grazed: the vegetation vanished, the wind got a grip on the cover sand, and whole fields and even farmsteads were buried. The planting of Scots pine from around 1900 was an emergency measure to fix the sand. It is now a varied wood with old pines, broadleaves and glades. Black woodpecker, woodlark and nightjar breed, and slow worm and common lizard live here.

tags: Heide · heideveld met vennen op dekzand
nl.location: 📍 Bij Arriën, ten oosten van Ommen · Heideveld · Middelgroot
nl.description: Het Arriëveld is een heideveld op dekzand ten oosten van Ommen, met vennen in de laagtes. De vennen zijn er omdat het regenwater niet weg kan: onder het zand ligt een leemlaag die het water vasthoudt. Vennen zijn extreem voedselarm en zuur — er komt geen grondwater in, alleen regen, en regen bevat vrijwel geen voedingsstoffen. Dat maakt ze tot een van de meest kwetsbare habitats van Nederland: al een beetje extra stikstof uit de lucht verandert de vegetatie onherkenbaar. Waar het lukt de vennen schoon te houden groeien nog oeverkruid, veelstengelige waterbies en witte snavelbies. Er komen heikikker, gladde slang en boomleeuwerik voor.

tags: Heath · heathland with pools on cover sand
en.location: 📍 Near Arriën, east of Ommen · Heathland · Medium-sized
en.description: The Arriëveld is a heath on cover sand east of Ommen, with pools in the hollows. The pools exist because rainwater cannot drain away: beneath the sand lies a loam layer that holds it. Such pools are extremely nutrient-poor and acid — no groundwater enters, only rain, and rain contains almost no nutrients. That makes them one of the most vulnerable habitats in the Netherlands: even a little extra airborne nitrogen changes the vegetation beyond recognition. Where the pools can be kept clean, shoreweed, many-stalked spike-rush and white beak-sedge still grow. Moor frog, smooth snake and woodlark occur.

nl.location: 📍 Bij Junne, in het Vechtdal · Stroomdalgrasland · Klein
nl.description: Het Junner Koeland is een van de kostbaarste stukjes natuur van Overijssel: een eeuwenoude gemeenschappelijke weide in een bocht van de Vecht, waar de boeren van Junne al sinds de middeleeuwen hun vee lieten grazen. Zo’n gemeenschappelijk gebruikt terrein heette een marke, en het is uitzonderlijk dat het hier nooit is verdeeld of bemest. Daardoor is de bodem nog steeds voedselarm en kalkrijk — de Vecht bracht bij overstromingen kalkhoudend zand aan — en groeit er zeldzame stroomdalflora die elders in Nederland vrijwel is verdwenen. en.description: The Junner Koeland is one of the most precious patches of nature in Overijssel: a centuries-old common pasture in a bend of the Vecht, where the farmers of Junne have grazed their cattle since the Middle Ages. Such commonly used ground was called a marke, and it is exceptional that this one was never divided or fertilised. The soil is therefore still nutrient-poor and lime-rich — the Vecht brought calcareous sand during floods — and rare river-valley flora grows here that has all but vanished elsewhere in the Netherlands. Maiden pink, field eryngo and wild thyme flower. The area is still grazed, nowadays by cattle.

en.location: 📍 Stegeren, between Ommen and Hardenberg · Riverbank and estate · Medium-sized
en.description: At Stegeren the Vecht has undergone one of the most successful remeandering projects in the Netherlands. The river was straightened in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries to let boats through and drain water quickly; the result was a canal with uniform flow everywhere and almost no life left in it. Since the 2000s old meanders have been reopened and the river left free again to form sandbanks and steep banks. It worked fast: within a few years sand martin, little ringed plover and kingfisher returned, and the beaver settled. Around it lie the woods and avenues of the old Stegeren estate.

en.description: Around the hamlet of Stegeren lies a small-scale mosaic of hedgebanks, coppice copses, orchards and steep banks. The name derives from steger or landing stage — a mooring or fordable spot on the river, revealing that a Vecht crossing lay here early on. The hedgebanks follow the old parcel boundaries, some going back to the medieval division of the marke; they are thus among the few still legible traces of how the land was shared out centuries ago. Ecologically they are the skeleton of the area: badger, little owl, yellowhammer and slow worm use them as habitat and as a link between the woods and the Vecht valley.

en.location: 📍 Junne, east of Ommen · Estate and river valley · Medium-sized
en.description: Junne is a hamlet of barely a handful of farms in a great bend of the Vecht, and one of the best-preserved Vecht valley landscapes. The whole area belongs to an estate that remained in one hand for centuries, which explains why the scaling-up that transformed the rest of Overijssel largely passed it by: there were no land consolidations, the hedgebanks stayed, the arable domes were never levelled. The result is a landscape now rarely seen in the Netherlands: essen, hay meadows, river dunes and old oaks in their original coherence. Badger, kingfisher, golden oriole, beaver and rare river-valley flora occur.

en.description: Ommen received town rights in 1248 and owes its existence to a ford in the Vecht: here the river was shallow enough to cross, and where a trade route crosses a river a settlement with toll, market and inn arises of its own accord. Op de hoogste zandruggen liggen de essen, in het dal de hooilanden, en daartussen liggen restanten stuifzand — het gevolg van eeuwen overbelasting van de heide. Bijzonder is de Beerzerbelten: een stuifzandgebied waar de wind het zand tot heuse duinen heeft opgeworpen. Zulke landduinen zijn een uitgesproken Europees zeldzaam verschijnsel; ze bestaan alleen waar zand, wind en menselijke overexploitatie samenkwamen. Op het open zand leven zandhagedis, boomleeuwerik en heivlinder, en ’s avonds jaagt de nachtzwaluw.

en.location: 📍 Beerze, between Ommen and Mariënberg · Es village and sand landscape · Medium-sized
en.description: Beerze is a small es village on the Vecht with a landscape that carries the whole story of the sandy soils. The essen lie on the highest sand ridges, the hay meadows in the valley, and between them lie remnants of drift sand — the result of centuries of overburdening the heath. Remarkable are the Beerzerbelten: a drift-sand area where the wind has thrown the sand up into genuine dunes. Such inland dunes are a distinctly rare European phenomenon; they exist only where sand, wind and human overexploitation came together. Sand lizard, woodlark and grayling butterfly live on the open sand, and the nightjar hunts at dusk.

tags: Estate · castle with baroque avenue system
en.location: 📍 Eerde, west of Ommen · Estate · Large
en.description: Eerde estate, with its castle of 1715 and its system of avenues, is one of the most intact baroque estate layouts in the Netherlands. The main axis runs straight for kilometres: that is not decoration but a display of power from the age of Louis XIV, in which the landscape was forced into geometry to show that the owner mastered nature. In the nineteenth century the looser English landscape style was added in the outer margins, so that the estate shows two opposed design philosophies side by side. Ecologically the centuries-old beeches and oaks are valuable: bats, pine marten, tawny owl, stock dove and rare bracket fungi live in the old timber.

en.description: Het Laar is an old estate park near Ommen, and the name is one of the oldest landscape words in the Netherlands. A laar meant in Old Dutch an open place in the wood where livestock was pastured — a wood pasture. The word recurs in dozens of place names (Laren, Elspeet-Laar, Wenslaar) and dates from a time when most of the Netherlands was still forest and such clearings were exceptional enough to name. The present park is nineteenth-century, with winding paths, ponds and specimen trees in the English landscape style. The old trees offer nest cavities to tawny owl, stock dove, nuthatch and summer roosts to bats.

en.description: Giethmen is an es village on the sandy soils between Ommen and the Lemelerberg, with a large communal es still in use as open arable land. Such open essen have become rare: in most places they have been parcelled, built on or edged with trees, so that the characteristic wide view vanished. The es of Giethmen still shows what such communal arable looked like — gently domed by centuries of sod manuring, without fences, with the farms at the rim. Around it lie hedgebanks, coppice and heath remnants. Badger, little owl, skylark and grey partridge occur — species dependent on precisely this old landscape type.

Een stuwwal is geen gewone heuvel maar het werk van landijs: tijdens de voorlaatste ijstijd, zo’n 150.000 jaar geleden, schoof een gletsjertong de bodemlagen als een bulldozer opzij en omhoog. tags: Ice-pushed ridge · heath and drift sand on a glacial ridge
en.location: 📍 Between Lemele, Archem and Hellendoorn · Ice-pushed ridge with heath · Large
en.description: The Lemelerberg and the Archemerberg together form one of the finest ice-pushed ridges in Overijssel. Such a ridge is no ordinary hill but the work of land ice: during the penultimate ice age, some 150,000 years ago, a glacier tongue shoved the soil layers aside and upward like a bulldozer. The tilted, pushed-up sand and clay layers can still be seen in exposures. At over 75 metres the Lemelerberg offers views across half of Salland. Extensive heath with drift sand lies on the flanks, managed with a sheep flock. Sand lizard, smooth snake, nightjar and woodlark live here, and rare juniper scrub grows.

en.location: 📍 Archem, between Ommen and Lemele · Hamlet with woodland · Medium-sized
en.description: Archem lies at the foot of the Archemerberg, and that position explains everything about the landscape. At the edge of an ice-pushed ridge, the rainwater that sank into the high sand ridge returns to the surface as seepage — clear, cool, mineral-rich groundwater flowing all year round. Such seepage zones at the foot of hill ridges are among the richest places in the Dutch sand landscape: the soil there is more fertile and moister than on the dry ridge above. That is where the hay meadows and brooks arose, and where the first farmers settled. Marsh marigold, water violet and orchids grow, and badger, kingfisher and brook invertebrates live here.

en.location: 📍 Near Lemele, at the foot of the Lemelerberg · Farmstead and land · Small
en.description: Ten Have is an old farmstead with its attendant land at the foot of the Lemelerberg. The name is telling: have means property or livestock — the same stem as in the Dutch phrase have en goed — and points to a medieval holding. Such old farmsteads are ecologically more important than their size suggests. Around a centuries-old yard there are always pollarded willows, standard fruit trees, hedgebanks and pools, and in the barns and hollow trees sit little owl, barn owl, bats and barn swallow. Those species depend entirely on farmyards — with the modernisation of agriculture their nest sites disappeared en masse. Restored yards like this are therefore key sites in the farmland nature network.

en.description: Park 1813 in Ommen owes its name to the year the Netherlands freed itself from French rule. At the centenary commemoration in 1913, memorial parks and woods were laid out all over the country — a typically nineteenth- and early twentieth-century way of fixing history in the landscape, in the same spirit as the Wilhelmina woods and Juliana avenues. The park is laid out in landscape style, with winding paths and tree clumps, and abuts the Vecht. The now century-old trees provide nest cavities and dead wood: great spotted woodpecker, nuthatch and stock dove breed, and bats hunt here at dusk.

en.location: 📍 Near Diffelen, in the Vecht valley · Drift sand and heath · Medium-sized
en.description: De Zandstuve is a drift-sand area in the Vecht valley, and the name leaves little to the imagination: here the sand blew. The river dunes along the Vecht lost their vegetation in the late Middle Ages through grazing and sod-cutting, after which the wind had free rein. The result was a sand drift that threatened villages and fields — a landscape disaster contemporaries experienced as a plague. Today that very open sand is managed as a natural value, for drift sand has become one of the rarest habitats in Europe. On the bare sand live sand lizard, blue-winged grasshopper and tiger beetles, and grey hair-grass and lichens grow.

en.location: 📍 Around Daarle, between Hellendoorn and Vriezenveen · Small elements · Small
en.description: Around Daarle lies one of the finest hedgebank landscapes in Overijssel. This is the transition from Salland to Twente, and Twente is known for its small-scale coulisse landscape: fields and meadows edged by hedgebanks and tree lines, so that the landscape opens as a series of stage wings one behind the other. That is no aesthetic design but a consequence of inheritance law on the sandy soils, where farms worked with small, scattered parcels each of which had to be screened separately against straying livestock. What remains is a network full of edges and cover: badger, little owl, red-backed shrike, yellowhammer and many butterflies and bees.

nl.description: De Engbertsdijksvenen zijn een van de laatste plekken in Nederland waar nog levend hoogveen groeit. Levend hoogveen is een uitzonderlijk verschijnsel: het bestaat vrijwel geheel uit veenmos, dat aan de bovenkant doorgroeit terwijl het aan de onderkant afsterft en niet verteert omdat het water zuur en zuurstofloos is. Zo stapelt de plant zichzelf op tot een veenkussen dat boven het grondwater uitgroeit en uitsluitend van regenwater leeft — vandaar hoog-veen. Groeisnelheid: ongeveer een millimeter per jaar. tags: Raised bog · one of the last living raised bogs in the Netherlands
en.location: 📍 Near Vriezenveen and Kloosterhaar · Raised bog · Large
en.description: The Engbertsdijksvenen are one of the last places in the Netherlands where living raised bog still grows. Living raised bog is an exceptional phenomenon: it consists almost entirely of sphagnum moss, which grows on at the top while dying at the bottom without decaying, because the water is acid and oxygen-free. So the plant piles itself up into a bog cushion that grows above the groundwater and lives purely on rainwater — hence raised bog. Growth rate: about a millimetre a year. Recovery after centuries of peat cutting therefore demands large-scale rewetting. Cranes breed here, and moor frog, smooth snake and rare bog dragonflies live here.

Een haar is in het oosten van Nederland een langgerekte zandrug — hetzelfde woord dat terugkomt in Kloosterhaar en tientallen veldnamen — en bruin verwijst naar de kleur van het veen dat eromheen lag. Zo’n zandrug midden in het veen was van grote waarde: het was de enige begaanbare route door een verder ondoordringbaar moeras, en er liepen dan ook oude veenwegen overheen. Nu ligt hier een mozaïek van natte heide, berkenbroek en veenrestanten, dat als bufferzone voor het hoogveen wordt vernat. Er leven heikikker, adder, gladde slang en broeden wulp en roodborsttapuit.

tags: Bog remnant · wet heath and wood on a cover-sand ridge
en.location: 📍 Near Kloosterhaar, eastern Overijssel · Bog and heath · Medium-sized
en.description: De Bruine Haar adjoins the Engbertsdijksvenen and bears a name that literally describes the landscape. A haar is, in the east of the Netherlands, an elongated sand ridge — the same word recurring in Kloosterhaar and dozens of field names — and bruin (brown) refers to the colour of the peat that lay around it. Such a ridge in the middle of the bog was of great value: it was the only passable route through an otherwise impenetrable marsh, and old bog roads accordingly ran across it. Now a mosaic of wet heath, birch carr and bog remnants lies here, being rewetted as a buffer zone for the raised bog. Moor frog, adder and smooth snake live here, and curlew and stonechat breed.

tags: Country estates · parks on the beach ridge along the Spaarne
en.location: 📍 Heemstede, along the Spaarne · Estate parks · Small
en.description: Along the Spaarne near Heemstede lies a series of old estate parks: Bosbeek, the Burgemeester Rijkenspark and the Spaarneberg. All three sit on a beach ridge — an old, elevated sand ridge that functioned as the coastline five thousand years ago and now lies kilometres inland. That combination of high, dry sandy ground and nearness to water made the strip attractive to Amsterdam merchants, who from the seventeenth century built their country houses here, a short tow-barge journey from the city. The old trees are now ecologically valuable: nuthatch, great spotted woodpecker, stock dove, bats and rare stinzen flora that arrived with the landscaping.

en.description: Schapenduinen in Bloemendaal lies on the inner dune edge, and the name refers to the old use of the dunes as sheep pasture. Before the dunes became nature reserves they were common grazing land for centuries: villages at the dune foot ran their sheep there, which kept the vegetation short and let the sand drift locally. That grazing determined the open dune landscape we now regard as natural — without livestock, dunes grow over with scrub. On the estate dune woodland, grasslands and old avenues now alternate. Nightingale, nuthatch and green woodpecker breed, and rare orchids grow on the lime-rich dune soil.

en.location: 📍 Bloemendaal, inner dune edge · Dune wood · Small
en.description: The Bloemendaalsebos is an old broadleaf wood on the inner dune edge, and it is precisely that position which makes it special. The inner dune edge is the narrow strip where the dune passes into the lower hinterland: here the soil is lime-rich but sheltered, rainfall is sufficient and there is no salt wind. That is the most favourable combination in the entire dune region, and it explains why woodland could grow here while the dune itself is too dry and windy for it. Moreover, seepage water that sank through the dune sand surfaces at the inner edge. The wood holds nuthatch, tawny owl, great spotted woodpecker and a rich spring flora.

tags: Native plant garden · the first heemtuin in the Netherlands
en.location: 📍 Bloemendaal, inner dune edge · Native plant garden · Very small
en.description: Thijsse’s Hof is the first heemtuin in the Netherlands, laid out in 1925 as a gift to the nature teacher and writer Jac. P. Thijsse. The idea behind it was revolutionary: instead of displaying exotic ornamentals, a garden would show the native plant communities of its own region, arranged by soil type — dune grassland beside dune wood beside damp hollow. Any city dweller could thus see in half an hour how the nature of his own surroundings fitted together. The concept has been imitated worldwide ever since. On barely two hectares hundreds of native species grow, with orchids, Solomon’s seal and ramsons, and nightingale, garden warbler and blackcap breed.

en.location: 📍 Buitenhuizen, near Spaarnwoude · Scour pool · Very small
en.description: A braak is no ordinary pool but a dike-breach scour hole: the pit left behind when a dike gives way and the inrushing water scours a deep hollow with enormous force. Such holes are often ten to twenty metres deep — far deeper than the surrounding ditches — and because they were too deep to fill in they simply remained after the dike was repaired. The Buitenhuizerbraak thus recalls a flood of the IJ, centuries ago. Because of their depth and steep banks, breach pools have an ecology of their own: cold, clear water with species absent from shallow polder pools. Great crested grebe and little grebe breed, and the banks hold reedbed birds.

en.description: The Houtrakbos forms part of Spaarnwoude, one of the first large buffer zones in the Netherlands. The wood is now mature: goshawk, buzzard, great spotted woodpecker and kingfisher breed, and the many pools attract dragonflies and waterfowl.

en.description: The Spaarnwouderveen is one of the few surviving peat remnants in this greatly altered area between Amsterdam and Haarlem, and beside it lies a battery of the Defence Line of Amsterdam. That battery formed part of a 135-kilometre defensive ring built around the capital between 1880 and 1920, based on a single principle: at the threat of attack the surrounding land would be flooded to a depth of roughly thirty to fifty centimetres — too shallow for boats, too deep and muddy for infantry and artillery. The fort itself is now a bat hibernation site; meadow birds breed on the peat and marsh flora grows.

en.location: 📍 Along the Liede near Haarlem · Riverside land · Small
en.description: The Liede is one of the oldest watercourses in North Holland: a natural peat river that existed before humans reclaimed the area. The name is related to leede, a watercourse that leads water away — the same word contained in Leiden and dozens of other place names. Before the Haarlemmermeer was drained, the Liede connected the peat district with the IJ, and for centuries the river determined where people could live and sail. Along the banks now lie reed fringes, rough vegetation and wet grasslands. Sedge warbler, reed warbler, bluethroat and marsh harrier breed there, and the grass snake has been recorded.
